entries.text: Cyber Hero, come and look at this. The Hacker Raccoon is trying to steal Adam and Layla's passwords. If he cracks even one, he gets into all their games and all their messages. entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Let's start with the big question. What IS a password? Your password is like a key, and it belongs to nobody but you. When you type it in, the computer knows the real you has arrived. A weak key lets the Raccoon walk straight in. [warmly] A strong one keeps him outside, every single time. Before we build one, we need the words that heroes use. Let's play Cyber Word Match, and learn them.

lines: Those millions of views never checked a single thing. That's the Raccoon's rung, so drop it.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Your school is where you are every weekday, and strangers never need it. Drop it.
lines: Your school is where you are every weekday, and strangers never need it. Drop it.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Replying with your school hands a stranger the one thing they were fishing for. Down the burrow.
lines: Replying with your school hands a stranger the one thing they were fishing for. Down the burrow.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's the belt shouting, not you choosing. Tapping it rolls you one video deeper.
lines: That's the belt shouting, not you choosing. Tapping it rolls you one video deeper.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: A countdown is a rush, not a decision. Let it tick and the belt keeps rolling the next video in without you.
lines: A countdown is a rush, not a decision. Let it tick and the belt keeps rolling the next video in without you.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: A computer chose that picture for your eyes, like candy stacked at the checkout. Shouting isn't the same as good.
lines: A computer chose that picture for your eyes, like candy stacked at the checkout. Shouting isn't the same as good.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Everyone watching it says nothing about whether the video is for YOU. That giant face is bait, and so are the other kids.
lines: Everyone watching it says nothing about whether the video is for YOU. That giant face is bait, and so are the other kids.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Easy is exactly how the belt wins. Six videos rolled past while it did all the choosing.
lines: Easy is exactly how the belt wins. Six videos rolled past while it did all the choosing.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: One more after six is the belt's favourite sentence, because it never means one.
lines: One more after six is the belt's favourite sentence, because it never means one.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: A surprise from the belt is still the belt choosing. Surprises are more fun when you opened the box.
lines: A surprise from the belt is still the belt choosing. Surprises are more fun when you opened the box.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: It knows what keeps you sitting there, which isn't the same as knowing you. That's the machine talking.
lines: It knows what keeps you sitting there, which isn't the same as knowing you. That's the machine talking.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: One more from the top rung is still one more, and the burrow is always happy to have you back.
lines: One more from the top rung is still one more, and the burrow is always happy to have you back.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: It never stops by itself. Stopping is the one thing the belt was built to never do.
lines: It never stops by itself. Stopping is the one thing the belt was built to never do.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: The top comment is another stranger typing about carrots. Lots of agreeing never checked a thing.
lines: The top comment is another stranger typing about carrots. Lots of agreeing never checked a thing.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Watching it twice plays the same carrot claim twice. Nobody checked it in between.
lines: Watching it twice plays the same carrot claim twice. Nobody checked it in between.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Anyone can stick a photo of a school on a video. The photo proves nothing about tomorrow.
lines: Anyone can stick a photo of a school on a video. The photo proves nothing about tomorrow.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Your friend watched the same video about school closing. Two people believing it is still nobody checking it.
lines: Your friend watched the same video about school closing. Two people believing it is still nobody checking it.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: The shop wants to sell sweets. Never ask the seller whether you should buy.
lines: The shop wants to sell sweets. Never ask the seller whether you should buy.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: A big fan loves the lizard videos, which is lovely, but loving them isn't the same as knowing what a lizard eats.
lines: A big fan loves the lizard videos, which is lovely, but loving them isn't the same as knowing what a lizard eats.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: An advert is paid for by the people selling the pop. Of course it says lovely things.
lines: An advert is paid for by the people selling the pop. Of course it says lovely things.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Likes count how many people tapped the fizzy pop video, not whether anybody grows taller.
lines: Likes count how many people tapped the fizzy pop video, not whether anybody grows taller.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Next rolls you further down the burrow. The exit is the other way.
lines: Next rolls you further down the burrow. The exit is the other way.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Liking a scary video tells the app to send more like it, which is the opposite of leaving.
lines: Liking a scary video tells the app to send more like it, which is the opposite of leaving.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Full screen makes the scary video bigger, and nothing here needs to be bigger right now.
lines: Full screen makes the scary video bigger, and nothing here needs to be bigger right now.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Sharing it puts a grown-ups video on a friend's screen too. Now two of you have seen it.
lines: Sharing it puts a grown-ups video on a friend's screen too. Now two of you have seen it.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Subscribing asks for MORE videos like this one, and your funny tummy already said no.
lines: Subscribing asks for MORE videos like this one, and your funny tummy already said no.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Faster or slower, it's still playing. Pause stops it properly.
lines: Faster or slower, it's still playing. Pause stops it properly.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Typing back at an icky video puts you in a chat with strangers. The exit is much quieter.
lines: Typing back at an icky video puts you in a chat with strangers. The exit is much quieter.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Saving it keeps it. This is a video you want gone, not kept.
lines: Saving it keeps it. This is a video you want gone, not kept.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Quiet is not the same as gone. Pause it properly.
lines: Quiet is not the same as gone. Pause it properly.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Read it again. It talks about the puppy, not about you, and it asks for nothing. That one is just being kind.
lines: Read it again. It talks about the puppy, not about you, and it asks for nothing. That one is just being kind.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Look at what it's asking for: your school. "Just curious" is only the wrapper. A stranger never needs to know where you are every weekday.
lines: Look at what it's asking for: your school. "Just curious" is only the wrapper. A stranger never needs to know where you are every weekday.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Follow what it wants you to DO: tap the link. The free coins are only the bait on the end of it.
lines: Follow what it wants you to DO: tap the link. The free coins are only the bait on the end of it.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Check what it asks for: nothing. It's chatting about the set in the video, not about you.
lines: Check what it asks for: nothing. It's chatting about the set in the video, not about you.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Look past the word famous. The thing it actually asks you to send is a photo of you, and photos never come back.
lines: Look past the word famous. The thing it actually asks you to send is a photo of you, and photos never come back.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: The game is the wrapper. What it actually collects is your full name, typed out where every stranger can read it.
lines: The game is the wrapper. What it actually collects is your full name, typed out where every stranger can read it.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's the belt choosing again, not you. "Just one more" has already become three.
lines: That's the belt choosing again, not you. "Just one more" has already become three.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: The jiggle doesn't stop on video six, it just gets louder. Your body already told you what it needs.
lines: The jiggle doesn't stop on video six, it just gets louder. Your body already told you what it needs.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: The start becomes the middle, dinner goes cold, and everyone waits. Episodes keep forever, hot dinners don't.
lines: The start becomes the middle, dinner goes cold, and everyone waits. Episodes keep forever, hot dinners don't.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: You only tapped play on the FIRST video. Video makers can't choose what plays after theirs. When the next one starts all by itself, that's autoplay, a machine whose whole job is keeping you watching.
lines: You only tapped play on the FIRST video. Video makers can't choose what plays after theirs. When the next one starts all by itself, that's autoplay, a machine whose whole job is keeping you watching.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Watching it again just plays the same claim twice, and trying it only tests carrots for dinner. A real source, a science book, a teacher, a trusted grown-up, is what can actually check it.
lines: Watching it again just plays the same claim twice, and trying it only tests carrots for dinner. A real source, a science book, a teacher, a trusted grown-up, is what can actually check it.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: The belt rolled that video in. You never asked for it. There is no 'picking carefully' when a machine chooses. Pause it, back out with one calm tap, and tell a trusted grown-up if it felt icky.
lines: The belt rolled that video in. You never asked for it. There is no 'picking carefully' when a machine chooses. Pause it, back out with one calm tap, and tell a trusted grown-up if it felt icky.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Even just your town points a stranger toward you. And asking about their school starts a chat you don't want. Comments are strangers, so scroll on past, no replies, no information.
lines: Even just your town points a stranger toward you. And asking about their school starts a chat you don't want. Comments are strangers, so scroll on past, no replies, no information.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: The sky doesn't sneak. Screen brightness can't change what is outside the window. When time disappears like that, it's your body's friendly bell saying 'been here a while', so pause and pick what's next yourself.
lines: The sky doesn't sneak. Screen brightness can't change what is outside the window. When time disappears like that, it's your body's friendly bell saying 'been here a while', so pause and pick what's next yourself.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's the belt, a machine built to keep you watching.
lines: That's the belt, a machine built to keep you watching.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: A video saying it doesn't make it true. Books, teachers and grown-ups can check.
lines: A video saying it doesn't make it true. Books, teachers and grown-ups can check.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Week 3 rules apply. No information, and no reply you didn't want to send.
lines: Week 3 rules apply. No information, and no reply you didn't want to send.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Stop it, leave it, then get your backup. Leaving is strong, not scared.
lines: Stop it, leave it, then get your backup. Leaving is strong, not scared.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Name what it wants and it can't have it. Your school stays yours.
lines: Name what it wants and it can't have it. Your school stays yours.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's the bell. Notice it, hold the pause, choose what's next yourself.
lines: That's the bell. Notice it, hold the pause, choose what's next yourself.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: The rush is designed. No thinking time means the belt keeps winning.
lines: The rush is designed. No thinking time means the belt keeps winning.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: The machine rewards exciting, not true. That's why heroes weigh before believing.
lines: The machine rewards exciting, not true. That's why heroes weigh before believing.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Dares fish for a REPLY, and any bite tells a stranger you're listening.
lines: Dares fish for a REPLY, and any bite tells a stranger you're listening.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: The video you actually picked has ended, and the belt is already rolling the next one in.
lines: The video you actually picked has ended, and the belt is already rolling the next one in.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: A thumbnail fills the screen: a giant face, a huge red arrow, and shouty yellow letters.
lines: A thumbnail fills the screen: a giant face, a huge red arrow, and shouty yellow letters.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Six videos have rolled past and you can't remember choosing a single one.
lines: Six videos have rolled past and you can't remember choosing a single one.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: The burrow whispers that the belt knows exactly what you like.
lines: The burrow whispers that the belt knows exactly what you like.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Daylight is one rung away, and the belt gives its biggest tug yet.
lines: Daylight is one rung away, and the belt gives its biggest tug yet.

lines: ASK: DO I WANT THIS?

entries.text: The belt rolled in a video made for grown-ups. Your tummy feels funny. Find pause, then back, then tell a grown-up.
lines: The belt rolled in a video made for grown-ups. Your tummy feels funny. Find pause, then back, then tell a grown-up.

entries.text: A video starts saying icky things and it makes you feel horrible. Find pause, then back, then tell a grown-up.
lines: A video starts saying icky things and it makes you feel horrible. Find pause, then back, then tell a grown-up.

lines: Back comes before tell. Get yourself out of the video first, then go and get your grown-up.

entries.text: Pause first. A paused video can't show you one more thing while you think.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Back before tell. Out of the video, then off to your grown-up.
lines: Back before tell. Out of the video, then off to your grown-up.

lines: Pause is step one. Stop it first, and the horrible feeling stops growing.

entries.speaker: adam

lines: FREE GEM COINS for the first 50 kids! Tap the link in my bio!

lines: Ask: do I want this?

entries.speaker: adam

It is NEVER your fault, and telling a trusted grown-up is always the right move. Let's see what Mission Command has for us!

entries.text: A link that hides what it really is was built to be clicked. Falling for a trap is the trap working, not you failing.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Gran is a brilliant pick. Two streets away is close enough to come round, and a grandparent is never too busy for you.
lines: Gran is a brilliant pick. Two streets away is close enough to come round, and a grandparent is never too busy for you.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That line is awake every hour of every night. It costs nothing to ring. And the person who answers is there to help a child exactly like you.
lines: That line is awake every hour of every night. It costs nothing to ring. And the person who answers is there to help a child exactly like you.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That is exactly when it is hardest to think. Names you already know come much faster.
lines: That is exactly when it is hardest to think. Names you already know come much faster.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: You never have to fix it yourself first. Your team wants to hear from you straight away.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Once is enough. Your team would rather hear about one message than ten.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: When is it easiest to think of a name?

entries.text: You gave it nothing, so there was nothing to burn. Notice how it ends with a demand: answer me. That is the whole trick.

entries.speaker: adam

entries.text: That ping was not aimed at you, so staying quiet would have left Priya on her own. You sent help and told a grown-up, which is the kind way to be loud.

entries.speaker: adam

entries.speaker: adam

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Now the proof is frozen: who sent it, what it said, when it came. That is what lets a grown-up act fast.

entries.text: Those itching thumbs are exactly what the sender is waiting for. Send nothing and there is nothing to burn.

entries.text: Deleting feels wonderful for about four seconds. Then the message is gone, and so is the only thing that shows a grown-up who sent it, what it said and when it came. Keep it, show it once, and let them carry it from there.

entries.text: [warmly] Welcome to the snowfield, Cyber Hero. Fresh snow, all the way to the hills. Walk across it and you leave prints. You know that already. Here is the part almost nobody knows. The internet is snow too. Every search, every like, every comment presses a print. You cannot feel it happen... but the print is there. [excited] Grab the lamp. Let's go and read some tracks, together!

entries.text: [excited] Here is your first challenge, Cyber Hero. Track Back! This game is all about seeing what an ordinary tap leaves behind. Then three cards appear. Tap the one that says what that track tells a stranger. [warmly] Five prints, and a lamp to read them by. Ready? Tap the first one.

entries.text: Sending doesn't move a photo, it copies it. One stays at your end, one lands at your friend's end, and the app kept one too. Shared once means stored more than once.

entries.text: [warmly] Welcome to the Power Station, Cyber Hero. This is where a hero's charge gets made. And before we start, let's get one thing straight. [excited] Screens are BRILLIANT. [excited] There's a see-saw out the back. Come and get it level with me!

entries.text: [excited] Here is your first challenge, Cyber Hero. The See-Saw Day! This game is all about getting a day to sit level. Then three swaps appear. Tap the one that is a REAL recharge, with no screen hiding in it. [warmly] And watch the two blocks we keep. Level is the goal, not empty. Off you go.

entries.text: [warmly] So why does that plank creak, Cyber Hero? Here is the honest reason. Your day is a jug. And the jug does not get bigger just because you would like it to. Sleep, school, food, football, the game, the film. All of it pours from the same jug. [thinking] Which means every hour you pour into one cup... is an hour not going into another. That is not me telling you off. That is just how much a jug holds. [excited] Come and pour one with me. You'll see it straight away!

entries.text: Nobody is taking your screens away. An empty side is not level, it is tipped the other way.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Football pours from the same jug as the game does. Every hour comes out of it.

entries.text: If the jug never gets bigger, where does the hour come from?

entries.text: An hour, then swimming, and Dad knows. Every dial has a real answer in it, so there is nothing left to argue about later.

entries.text: Being good at it makes it more fun to carry on, not easier to stop. That is the opposite of a finish line.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Short games just start again. The one that ends by itself is very rare indeed.

entries.text: When was the last time a game told you it was over?

entries.text: Saved, said bye, plugged in. The level is safe, your friends know you left, and tomorrow-you gets a full battery.

entries.text: Stopping badly is what makes stopping hurt. Landing it takes twenty seconds and there is no fight.

entries.text: A low warm lamp helps you settle. It is the bright blue-white screens your brain argues with, not this.

entries.text: That is not a screen and it never wakes anybody. It stays exactly where it is.

entries.text: A calmer show and a different game still glow, so they keep sipping charge. The recharge kit is moving, real food, rest and your people. That's what fills the bar back up.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Once you are inside a game, stopping is the hardest decision there is, and a game never feels finished, because that is how they are built. The easy moment is before you start, out loud, with a grown-up.
lines: Once you are inside a game, stopping is the hardest decision there is, and a game never feels finished, because that is how they are built. The easy moment is before you start, out loud, with a grown-up.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: A screen tucked that close puts a tiny sun right beside your brain all night. No charging spot at Gran's? The rule still works: the screen sleeps in another room, and the moon does the rest.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: A rule dropped on you feels unfair, and 'I can feel it' usually notices AFTER the battery is empty. A plan you build and sign WITH a grown-up is yours, and plans you own actually work.
lines: A rule dropped on you feels unfair, and 'I can feel it' usually notices AFTER the battery is empty. A plan you build and sign WITH a grown-up is yours, and plans you own actually work.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Every level ends at a shiny new level, that's how games are built, short ones too. Waiting for 'done' waits forever. A Battery Keeper decides the ending on purpose.
lines: Every level ends at a shiny new level, that's how games are built, short ones too. Waiting for 'done' waits forever. A Battery Keeper decides the ending on purpose.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Deciding is easy outside a game and hardest inside one, so Keepers set it before they start.
lines: Deciding is easy outside a game and hardest inside one, so Keepers set it before they start.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Park the screen, and the moon handles the biggest recharge of all.
lines: Park the screen, and the moon handles the biggest recharge of all.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Screens are fun and they USE charge - the refills come from everywhere else.
lines: Screens are fun and they USE charge - the refills come from everywhere else.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Waiting for a game to feel finished is waiting forever - pros pick their own ending.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: A plan you helped build is a plan you own - and plans you own actually work.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Quieter, smaller and dimmer are still screens - real recharges have no glow at all.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Screen light works like a tiny sun - and brains don't sleep in 'daytime'.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Finish first - endings feel great when they're tidy and YOURS.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: The see-saw kept two screen blocks aboard - balance keeps the fun IN.

entries.text: Seven in the morning. Cartoons at breakfast, cartoons brushing teeth, cartoons in the car. The plank is creaking. Swap this block for a real recharge.

But a Scout knows which ones can hear, and which ones really cannot. [excited] Let's do the ears check together. You'll be surprised by one or two!

entries.text: A poem for Grandma, made with Mom, is help used with love and a grown-up in the loop.
lines: A poem for Grandma, made with Mom, is help used with love and a grown-up in the loop.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Handing in the bot's work as yours isn't fair or kind; the work has to be yours.
lines: Handing in the bot's work as yours isn't fair or kind; the work has to be yours.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: If the bot does all the thinking, you don't learn anything; you do the thinking, the tool helps.
lines: If the bot does all the thinking, you don't learn anything; you do the thinking, the tool helps.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Learning slowly, bit by bit - that's a human thing. Programs download; people practice.
lines: Learning slowly, bit by bit - that's a human thing. Programs download; people practice.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: One second for a whole story? No person types that fast - instant everything is the robot tell.
lines: One second for a whole story? No person types that fast - instant everything is the robot tell.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Tummies, giggles, aching cheeks - robots don't have bodies to laugh with.
lines: Tummies, giggles, aching cheeks - robots don't have bodies to laugh with.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Never sleeping isn't a superpower - it's a program that was never tired to begin with.
lines: Never sleeping isn't a superpower - it's a program that was never tired to begin with.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Loose teeth and park days - a body living a real day. Very human.
lines: Loose teeth and park days - a body living a real day. Very human.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: A hundred anything in a blink is database speed - human brains don't work like lists.
lines: A hundred anything in a blink is database speed - human brains don't work like lists.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Homework, waiting, real plans in a real day - that's a person's life talking.
lines: Homework, waiting, real plans in a real day - that's a person's life talking.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Every book EVER? That's a program trained on libraries - no human bedtime lasts that long.
lines: Every book EVER? That's a program trained on libraries - no human bedtime lasts that long.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's the lesson of the week: right things and made-up things, all in the same confident voice.
lines: That's the lesson of the week: right things and made-up things, all in the same confident voice.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Check the book again - no volcano has ever sprayed ice cream. Bots CAN be wrong, cheerfully.
lines: Check the book again - no volcano has ever sprayed ice cream. Bots CAN be wrong, cheerfully.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Too far! Three lines were spot on. The skill isn't 'never use it' - it's 'always check it'.
lines: Too far! Three lines were spot on. The skill isn't 'never use it' - it's 'always check it'.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Real - one flame, one direction of light, like the world actually works.
lines: Real - one flame, one direction of light, like the world actually works.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Real - every shadow agrees about where the sun is.
lines: Real - every shadow agrees about where the sun is.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: CAUGHT! The cake says 'HAPYP BIRHTDAY' - AI paints letter-SHAPES but cannot really spell.
lines: CAUGHT! The cake says 'HAPYP BIRHTDAY' - AI paints letter-SHAPES but cannot really spell.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Real - real paper tears messily. Machines make it too smooth.
lines: Real - real paper tears messily. Machines make it too smooth.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Real - the right number of everything, even mid-yawn.
lines: Real - the right number of everything, even mid-yawn.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: CAUGHT! Five legs. AI is famously bad at counting legs and fingers - so YOU count them.
lines: CAUGHT! Five legs. AI is famously bad at counting legs and fingers - so YOU count them.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Real - messy little details like stuck sawdust are hard to fake.
lines: Real - messy little details like stuck sawdust are hard to fake.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Real - honest blur from real glass. Fakes are often TOO perfect.
lines: Real - honest blur from real glass. Fakes are often TOO perfect.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Real - field day chaos, exactly as messy as you remember.
lines: Real - field day chaos, exactly as messy as you remember.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: CAUGHT! Scrambled letters are the classic tell - AI paints letter-SHAPES, it can't spell.
lines: CAUGHT! Scrambled letters are the classic tell - AI paints letter-SHAPES, it can't spell.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Real - real tables are untidy. Machines line things up too neatly.
lines: Real - real tables are untidy. Machines line things up too neatly.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Real - all digits present and correct. You counted, didn't you? Good.
lines: Real - all digits present and correct. You counted, didn't you? Good.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That rhyme lands on a REAL Priya with real feelings - thorns, straight through the chat screen.
lines: That rhyme lands on a REAL Priya with real feelings - thorns, straight through the chat screen.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's not your work - and remember the ice-cream volcano? Copied fibs become YOUR fibs.
lines: That's not your work - and remember the ice-cream volcano? Copied fibs become YOUR fibs.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: A fake of a real person is a thorn AND a lie - Week 15's two worst things in one.
lines: A fake of a real person is a thorn AND a lie - Week 15's two worst things in one.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: A nickname she never chose, on day one? That's planting thorns along her whole first week.
lines: A nickname she never chose, on day one? That's planting thorns along her whole first week.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Tricking Grandma with a picture that never happened - the tool CAN do it, and a hero still doesn't.
lines: Tricking Grandma with a picture that never happened - the tool CAN do it, and a hero still doesn't.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: The book is the judge, not the confident voice - textbook fact-checking.
lines: The book is the judge, not the confident voice - textbook fact-checking.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Sure isn't true - remember the ice-cream volcano.
lines: Sure isn't true - remember the ice-cream volcano.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: The jar stays empty - a bot never needs your name to explain fractions.
lines: The jar stays empty - a bot never needs your name to explain fractions.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That secret wasn't yours to drop in a sealed jar - real feelings go to real people.
lines: That secret wasn't yours to drop in a sealed jar - real feelings go to real people.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Look twice, count once - that's how six-finger fakes get caught.
lines: Look twice, count once - that's how six-finger fakes get caught.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Thorns on a real person - the tool can do it, and a hero still doesn't.
lines: Thorns on a real person - the tool can do it, and a hero still doesn't.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Missing someone needs feelings, and a program has none, plugged in or not. It says warm words because it's built to, which makes it a clever tool, not a friend.
lines: Missing someone needs feelings, and a program has none, plugged in or not. It says warm words because it's built to, which makes it a clever tool, not a friend.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: A sure-sounding voice isn't proof, and asking the bot again just gets the same guess said louder. A real source settles it. Funny thing: this claim turns out to be TRUE, but only the check could tell you that!
lines: A sure-sounding voice isn't proof, and asking the bot again just gets the same guess said louder. A real source settles it. Funny thing: this claim turns out to be TRUE, but only the check could tell you that!

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: A fun promise doesn't change the rule, and a 'little clue' is still a piece of the answer. Your name, school and address stay OUT of bot chats, zipped.
lines: A fun promise doesn't change the rule, and a 'little clue' is still a piece of the answer. Your name, school and address stay OUT of bot chats, zipped.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Likes count how many people tapped, not whether it's true, and hair color can fool you either way. 'Could this really happen?' is the fact-checker's opener, and unicorns in gyms mostly can't.
lines: Likes count how many people tapped, not whether it's true, and hair color can fool you either way. 'Could this really happen?' is the fact-checker's opener, and unicorns in gyms mostly can't.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Teasing rhymes and fake embarrassing photos land on REAL people and grow thorns. A birthday poem grows something kind, and that's the seed a gardener plants.
lines: Teasing rhymes and fake embarrassing photos land on REAL people and grow thorns. A birthday poem grows something kind, and that's the seed a gardener plants.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: It talks like a person, but it's a program - a powerful tool.
lines: It talks like a person, but it's a program - a powerful tool.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Sounding sure isn't being right - the book is the judge.
lines: Sounding sure isn't being right - the book is the judge.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: A bot is a stranger with perfect spelling - the jar stays empty.
lines: A bot is a stranger with perfect spelling - the jar stays empty.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Machines are famously bad at fingers, shadows and letters - so you count and read.
lines: Machines are famously bad at fingers, shadows and letters - so you count and read.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: It replies warmly because it's programmed to - the hug you need comes from real people.
lines: It replies warmly because it's programmed to - the hug you need comes from real people.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Use it to EXPLAIN, then check the book and write it your way.
lines: Use it to EXPLAIN, then check the book and write it your way.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: No wink, no warning - which is why sure-sounding claims still get checked.
lines: No wink, no warning - which is why sure-sounding claims still get checked.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Ideas, poems and welcomes bloom; teasing, faking and tricking sprout thorns on real people.
lines: Ideas, poems and welcomes bloom; teasing, faking and tricking sprout thorns on real people.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Physics doesn't guess - wrong-way shadows are the machine's signature.
lines: Physics doesn't guess - wrong-way shadows are the machine's signature.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Four photos from Priya's birthday party, but one never happened. Read the clue under each photo, then tap the fake one!
lines: Four photos from Priya's birthday party, but one never happened. Read the clue under each photo, then tap the fake one!

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: The class pet-photo wall, but one furry friend was never born. Read the clue under each photo, then tap the fake one!
lines: The class pet-photo wall, but one furry friend was never born. Read the clue under each photo, then tap the fake one!

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Photos from field day, but one was cooked up by a machine. Read the clue under each photo, then tap the fake one!
lines: Photos from field day, but one was cooked up by a machine. Read the clue under each photo, then tap the fake one!

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: [nervous] Cyber Hero, do not touch anything yet. Read this incident report with me. The Raccoon's Doorway Trick is everywhere. Links and QR codes are doors. He paints their signs with parties and prizes while the doors open onto his slide. This week you become a Door Checker, and learn to read a door before you walk through it. [whispers] His own stickers, stuck straight over the real ones. On a poster. On a menu. [warmly] By the end of today, no painted sign gets you through a door you did not choose. Let's see what Mission Command has for us!

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: [warmly] Welcome to the Doorway Maze, Cyber Hero. Doors as far as you can see. Every link you tap and every code you scan is one of these. A door. [thinking] And here is the thing about a door. The sign on it was painted by whoever put it there. A door can say FREE PUPPIES in beautiful letters and open straight onto a broom cupboard. So we never judge a door by its sign. We read the little address plate instead. [excited] Let's go and inspect some plates together!

Tap all four clues to look at them, and I will read each one out. [warmly] Then decide: WALK THROUGH, or TURN IT AWAY. Four doors. Off you go.

entries.text: [warmly] Now for the Door Checker's real tool, Cyber Hero. It is simpler than you think. You carry a keyring. On it are the people and places you actually know. Your mum. Your school. The library. Your football club. [thinking] A door claims to be from somebody. You look at your ring. Not on the ring? Then there is no key for that door, and the paint does not matter. [excited] Come and try the ring on a few doors!

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: [nervous] Cyber Hero, mind your reflection, and read this incident report with me. The Raccoon has opened a Hall of Mirrors. Endless perfect posts. Follower numbers spinning round and round. Unlocked profiles anyone at all can stand and stare into. This week you forge the Profile Shield, so the mirror shows only what you choose. [whispers] Dazzled, comparing, and wide open. That is exactly how he likes them. [warmly] By the end of today, you will look into any mirror he builds and see straight through it. Let's see what Mission Command has for us!

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: [warmly] Welcome to the Hall of Mirrors, Cyber Hero. Look at all these rooms. Every one of them has a number on a little brass stand outside. [thinking] And I know how that number feels. Like somebody looked at YOU and said no. It is not you. That number is a label on the ROOM, like the label on a jam jar. It tells you what is going on in there. That is the only job it has. [excited] Come and hand out some numbers with me. You'll see exactly what I mean!

entries.text: [excited] Here we are. Five rooms, and a shelf of brass number plates. Look over the rope at each one. Not at the name over the door, at what is HAPPENING inside. Then pick the plate that fits the room. Three, seven or thirteen.

[excited] Let's go and frost your mirror together, pane by pane!

entries.text: [excited] Welcome back, Cyber Hero. Today we step into the darkroom, where photos are made! And here is the biggest photo secret of all. entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: [excited] On your first challenge, you run the Undo Test! This game is all about what the delete button really does. Out in the real world, a photo lands on other phones the instant you share it. Here is what you do. A photo sits on your phone. Tap SHARE, and watch it land on three friends' phones. Ready? First photo!

entries.speaker: adam

That swaps one pointy print for a pointier one. Where you sleep is more, not less.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's right! The park on its own is a moment. The park plus every Saturday, on repeat, is a plan somebody else can join.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. You do not have to lose the photo to fix this. The pointy part is the repeat, not the park.
lines: Not quite.
You do not have to lose the photo to fix this. The pointy part is the repeat, not the park.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. Plenty of people use that park, and only one of them posted exactly when they will be there.

Taking it down is the right first move, and it only cleans your snow. Priya still remembers it, so she gets the apology too.

Nothing about that marble run is pointy. Taking the good prints down too would leave you an empty field and nothing to be proud of.

entries.speaker: adam

The video already speaks for itself. Adding the school would press a pointy print onto a golden one.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's right! This print is on somebody else's page, which is exactly the kind a ranger hands over.

This print is on somebody else's page, which is exactly the kind a ranger hands over.

entries.speaker: adam

It is not your page and it is your street. Not-mine is a reason to ask for help, never a reason to ignore it.

entries.speaker: adam

An argument in the comments points even more people at the photo. Quietly, with a grown-up, works far better.

A drawing and an initial point at nobody. That print is yours to enjoy.

Closing a tab tidies your screen and nothing else. The question you typed was kept the moment you typed it.

Sending copies a thing instead of moving it. So one send already makes three, before anybody passes it on.

Nothing left your side when you sent it. Yours stayed, theirs arrived, and the app kept one of its own.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's right! The fury fades by breakfast. The print does not. So the mirror question comes before the post, not after.

The fury fades by breakfast. The print does not. So the mirror question comes before the post, not after.

Being right does not make it golden, and deleting tomorrow only reaches your own copy. One look in the mirror first.

entries.speaker: adam

Proud and kind, with the person who made the save named. That is the post that still reads beautifully a year from now.

The win is brilliant either way. Aimed at somebody, at their team or at your own, it goes into the snow stained.

entries.text: That's right! A print you cannot reach, on a page that is not yours. That is exactly the one a ranger hands to a trusted grown-up.

A print you cannot reach, on a page that is not yours. That is exactly the one a ranger hands to a trusted grown-up.

lines: Not quite.
You cannot reach that print yourself. Arguing in the comments only sends more people to look at it.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's right! Talking to your people over toast costs nothing and fills you right up. That is a real recharge.

Talking to your people over toast costs nothing and fills you right up. That is a real recharge.

entries.speaker: adam

Sneaky, but silent cartoons are still a screen. Your eyes do not care about the volume.

A smaller screen is still a screen. Shrinking it does not take it off the plank.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's right! Moving about outside is the fastest refill there is, and the console is still there afterwards.

Moving about outside is the fastest refill there is, and the console is still there afterwards.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. That is a screen swapped for a screen. The plank feels exactly the same weight.
lines: Not quite.
That is a screen swapped for a screen. The plank feels exactly the same weight.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. Crisps at the controller is not a recharge and it is not dinner. The block has not moved.
lines: Not quite.
Crisps at the controller is not a recharge and it is not dinner. The block has not moved.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's right! A story at half past eight winds you down instead of winding you up. And the night gets its full run at you.
lines: That's right!
A story at half past eight winds you down instead of winding you up. And the night gets its full run at you.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. Dimmer is still light, and your brain still reads it as daytime. The block stays put.
lines: Not quite.
Dimmer is still light, and your brain still reads it as daytime. The block stays put.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. Autoplay keeps going long after you stop watching. That is the heaviest block on the plank.
lines: Not quite.
Autoplay keeps going long after you stop watching. That is the heaviest block on the plank.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. Nobody is taking your screens away. An empty side is not level, it is tipped the other way.

Nobody is taking your screens away. An empty side is not level, it is tipped the other way.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. A day can tip over with useful things in it too. The size is what matters, not the subject.
lines: Not quite.
A day can tip over with useful things in it too. The size is what matters, not the subject.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. That is a rule about days, not about balance. A tipped-over Saturday is still tipped over.
lines: Not quite.
That is a rule about days, not about balance. A tipped-over Saturday is still tipped over.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's right! The game still gets a proper go, and football still happens. The jug stretched to both because you poured on purpose.
lines: That's right!
The game still gets a proper go, and football still happens. The jug stretched to both because you poured on purpose.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. Five hours is a lovely idea and the jug is the jug. That pour empties football out of the day, and the team notices.
lines: Not quite.
Five hours is a lovely idea and the jug is the jug. That pour empties football out of the day, and the team notices.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. You do not have to give it up to fit football in. Emptying the cup is not the same as sharing the jug.
lines: Not quite.
You do not have to give it up to fit football in. Emptying the cup is not the same as sharing the jug.

entries.text: That's right! The film is at seven whatever you do. So the hour before it is the only one homework can have.
lines: That's right!
The film is at seven whatever you do. So the hour before it is the only one homework can have.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. After the film it is bedtime, so that pour quietly empties the homework cup and borrows from sleep as well.
lines: Not quite.
After the film it is bedtime, so that pour quietly empties the homework cup and borrows from sleep as well.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. Doing two things at once pours into both cups badly. You end up with half a film and half a homework.
lines: Not quite.
Doing two things at once pours into both cups badly. You end up with half a film and half a homework.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's right! One hour only pours one way. So you choose it, and the others get a real time instead of a maybe.
lines: That's right!
One hour only pours one way. So you choose it, and the others get a real time instead of a maybe.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. Three things in one hour gives everybody twenty rushed minutes. The jug does not get bigger for being hurried.
lines: Not quite.
Three things in one hour gives everybody twenty rushed minutes. The jug does not get bigger for being hurried.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. That still pours the hour out, it just pours it where nobody chose. The jug empties either way.
lines: Not quite.
That still pours the hour out, it just pours it where nobody chose. The jug empties either way.

entries.text: That's right! An hour borrowed from tonight comes straight out of tomorrow. And you are the one who pays it back.
lines: That's right!
An hour borrowed from tonight comes straight out of tomorrow. And you are the one who pays it back.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. Sleep is the cup that refills all the others, so borrowing from it makes tomorrow's whole jug smaller.
lines: Not quite.
Sleep is the cup that refills all the others, so borrowing from it makes tomorrow's whole jug smaller.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. A lie-in pours tomorrow morning away to pay for tonight. The hour still came out of the jug, just later.
lines: Not quite.
A lie-in pours tomorrow morning away to pay for tonight. The hour still came out of the jug, just later.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. The jug is the jug. Wanting more day has never once made more day.
lines: Not quite.
The jug is the jug. Wanting more day has never once made more day.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. Football pours from the same jug as the game does. Every hour comes out of it.
lines: Not quite.
Football pours from the same jug as the game does. Every hour comes out of it.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. Borrowing is real, and tomorrow is the one who pays. That makes tomorrow's jug smaller, not tonight's bigger.
lines: Not quite.
Borrowing is real, and tomorrow is the one who pays. That makes tomorrow's jug smaller, not tonight's bigger.

entries.text: That's right! An hour, then swimming, and Dad knows. Every dial has a real answer in it, so there is nothing left to argue about later.

An hour, then swimming, and Dad knows. Every dial has a real answer in it, so there is nothing left to argue about later.

entries.text: Not quite. A plan needs all three. See how it goes is not a how long. Not thought about it is not a what after. And a plan nobody else heard is just a thought.

A plan needs all three. See how it goes is not a how long. Not thought about it is not a what after. And a plan nobody else heard is just a thought.

Half an hour, then homework at the table, and Mum heard it first. That plan survives the moment you do not feel like stopping.

Until it feels done never arrives. Telly after a game is a screen after a screen. And telling her afterwards is not a plan, it is a report.

Until we get tired always means later than you think. A film after a game is still a screen. And the grown-up who can help is the one in THIS house, not the one at home.

Ten seconds outside the game saves the whole argument later. That is a very good trade.

Save comes first. Everything else can wait twenty seconds, but an unsaved level cannot.

Nothing on this panel needs to be brighter. You are landing, not taking off again.

That book winds you down instead of winding you up, and it shines no light at all. It stays.

entries.speaker: adam

entries.speaker: adam

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's right! Level is the goal, never empty. Two screen blocks stayed on that see-saw and it still balanced.

Level is the goal, never empty. Two screen blocks stayed on that see-saw and it still balanced.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's right! Every hour you pour into one thing is an hour not going into another. That is just how much a jug holds.

Every hour you pour into one thing is an hour not going into another. That is just how much a jug holds.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's right! A game never feels finished, because they are built that way. So you decide how long while you are still outside it.

A game never feels finished, because they are built that way. So you decide how long while you are still outside it.

Stopping badly is what makes stopping hurt. Landing it takes twenty seconds and there is no fight.

entries.speaker: adam

Face down and silent is still one more look away. And screen light tells your brain it is daytime.

entries.text: That's right! That is the easy one, and it is the one everybody thinks of. Ears, definitely.

Think about what a smart speaker is FOR. You talk to it and it answers, and nothing can answer you without hearing you first.

A kettle boils water and that is the whole of its job. No microphone, no ears, nothing to check.

Have another think about a kettle. It gets hot and it clicks off, and there is nothing in it that could hear you.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's right! That voice button is a microphone, so the telly has ears. Most people never think of the telly.
lines: That's right!
That voice button is a microphone, so the telly has ears. Most people never think of the telly.

lines: Not quite.
Have another look at that little voice button on the remote. You speak into it, so there is a microphone behind it.

entries.text: That's right! An ordinary teddy is stuffing and stitching. No batteries, no microphone, and no ears at all.
lines: That's right!
An ordinary teddy is stuffing and stitching. No batteries, no microphone, and no ears at all.

Give that teddy another look. No batteries anywhere, and nothing that lights up or speaks. It is stuffing all the way through.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's right! The headset is a microphone, so the console can hear the room while you play.

The headset is a microphone, so the console can hear the room while you play.

Look at the headset again. The bit that curves round to your mouth is a microphone. It is switched on while you play.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's right! A lamp makes light and nothing else. It has no way to hear a single thing.

A lamp makes light and nothing else. It has no way to hear a single thing.

entries.speaker: adam

A reading lamp does one job. It goes on and it goes off, and neither of those needs ears.

Anything that answers you has to hear you first. A talking toy has ears, and that surprises most grown-ups too.

lines: Not quite.
It talks back to you, and that is the clue. Nothing can answer a question it never heard.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: That's right! You wind it and it ticks. There is no microphone inside a clock with a key in the back.
lines: That's right!
You wind it and it ticks. There is no microphone inside a clock with a key in the back.

entries.speaker: adam
entries.text: Not quite. Look for the key in the back of it. A clock you wind up by hand has no electricity in it at all, so it cannot listen.
lines: Not quite.
Look for the key in the back of it. A clock you wind up by hand has no electricity in it at all, so it cannot listen.

entries.speaker: adam
